translation_notes: Each prepareQuery(text, initNs=NAMESPACE_MAP) becomes s{ text }: NAMESPACE_MAP's odml:/rdf: bindings move to two module-level @prefix declarations, so the prologue is built once instead of passed to every call.
curr_graph.query(q) becomes q(curr_graph): the s{ } value is already the lazy prepared query prepareQuery used to build, so the call suffix replaces .query() directly.

The context reassigns q six times before the scored for-loop uses it; all six are translated (not just the last) since each is itself a sparql_literal occurrence, dead code or not -- translating only the used one would silently drop five instances of the construction under study.

Weak oracle: the extracted context builds curr_graph = Graph() but drops the original file's curr_graph.parse(FILE_PATH) call (out of the region's context lines), so the graph is empty on both sides and the loop body never runs. The check is still meaningful -- it proves s{ } parses at transpile time and that q(curr_graph) executes without error and yields the same (empty) result as curr_graph.query(q) -- but it does not exercise the FILTER/property-path/subquery machinery inside the query text against real data.
optimization_notes: The region is the final loop only (lines 86-88); the six prepared queries are header and stay byte for byte on both sides.
Both sides: the two concatenated f-strings of the print become one line. optimized.ldpy keeps `q(curr_graph)`; nothing else to compress.

The notation ratio (about 5.2) comes entirely from the header: the six queries are one string token each in Python and tokenized SPARQL in the s{ } islands of the translated header. The region lines differ only by `curr_graph.query(q)` against `q(curr_graph)`.
header_optimization_notes: Python and LD Python: the region (lines 86-88) reads only the last `q`. The first five `q = ...` assignments of the header are overwritten before the region runs, so they go on both sides: five prepareQuery(...) calls in Python and five s{ } islands in LD Python. This is the only header change in this batch that removes more than imports, and it is identical on both sides.

Python: Graph, prepareQuery and NAMESPACE_MAP stay, because the remaining query uses them. LD Python: only Graph is imported; the odml: and rdf: @prefix lines stay, because the remaining query uses them.
The header-variant notation ratio stays above 1 (about 3.0 against 5.2): in the remaining query, the SPARQL text is one string token in Python and tokenized SPARQL in s{ }.
